# Outline notes and delayed recall of technical prose

- **Citation:** Fictional Al Researcher, 2021, Journal of Made-Up Studies
- **Source file:** papers/sample/al-researcher-2021.pdf
- **Extracted:** 2026-09-19
- **Screening:** included after full text.

## Research question
Does outline-style note-taking improve 1-week recall of a technical article compared with free-form notes?

## Methods
Between-subjects laboratory experiment. Two groups read the same methods chapter and took notes in the assigned format, then completed a delayed free-recall test.

## Sample / data
N=40 undergraduates at one university.

## Claim-ready facts
- **Design:** between-subjects laboratory experiment
- **Population / model:** undergraduates, one university
- **n:** 40
- **Intervention / comparator:** outline notes vs free-form notes
- **Primary endpoint:** 1-week delayed free-recall score
- **Primary result:** outline group scored 18% higher (p<0.05)
- **Cannot show:** semester-long retention; STEM vs humanities

## Key findings
- Outline notes raised 1-week recall by 18% versus free-form notes (N=40; p<0.05).

## Limitations (as stated by the authors, or evident from the methods)
- Single institution; recall measured once.

## Relevance to our research question
Direct test of structured vs unstructured notes on technical recall.

## Open questions / things to verify
None after reading the PDF methods and Table 1.
